conventions.text: Volume fixing: [R] fixes Ñ4 = N41, the number of (4,1)+(1,4) simplices, by adding δS = ε|N41 − Ñ4| with ε = 0.01–0.02 (0.05 during thermalisation). κ4 is tuned to its pseudo-critical value to an accuracy of about 0.2ε.
sub: 3p1_mh uses the quadratic form EPS·(N41 − target)² instead. Both fix N41, so the ensembles agree up to the shape of the volume distribution, which is immaterial at fixed N41.

conventions.text: N3(i): the number of tetrahedra in the spatial slice at integer time i. Every spatial tetrahedron lies in exactly two (4,1)-type simplices, so ΣN3 = N41/2.
Sweep: 10⁶ attempted moves [R]. Their acceptance rate was about 12.5%. Thermalisation took between 10⁵ and 10⁸ sweeps, growing linearly with Ñ4.
Stalk: the average N41 per time step in the stalk is s ≈ 25.5, so N3 ≈ s/2 ≈ 12.75 per slice there. The minimum is 5 [R, Rev].
Centre of volume [dS, footnote 4]: minimise CV(i′) = |Σ_{i=−N/2}^{N/2−1} (i+0.5)·N3(1+mod(i′+i−1, N))| over i′. On ties take the i′ with the largest N3(i′). Then shift so that i_cv sits at 0.

items.label: A
items.text: (example κ0=5.0, Δ=0): an irregular sequence of maxima and minima in N3(τ), with extended stretches of only about Δτ ≈ 3.

items.label: B
items.text: (example κ0=1.6, Δ=0): all four-simplices sit in a slice of minimal time extension, Δτ = 2. N3 stays at its kinematic minimum everywhere else.

items.label: C
items.text: (κ0=2.2, Δ=0.6): an extended blob plus a stalk. The time extent scales as N4^{1/4} and the spatial volume as N4^{3/4}.

items.label: A–C transition
items.text: first order, at κ0 = 4.711 for Δ=0.6, N4 = 120k (Fig. 21 of [Rev]). The order parameter N0/N4 jumps between about 0.153 and 0.163.

items.label: B–C transition
items.text: second (or higher) order, at Δ = 0.022 for κ0=2.2, N4 = 40k (Fig. 22 of [Rev]). The order parameter is conj(Δ) = (N41 − 6N0)/N4. The peak separation shrinks about as 1/N4.

items.label: Qualitative phase diagram
items.text: ([Rev] Fig. 17): the B–C line rises from Δ≈0 at κ0≈1–2 toward the triple point. The A–C line is near κ0 ≈ 4–5 for Δ up to about 0.6–0.8.

targets.title: de Sitter profile ([dS] eq. 12–13, [Rev] eq. 220/224) at (2.2, 0.6), T=80
text: The fit holds inside the extended region only. s0 = 0.59, defined with the total N4; it was verified for N4 = 45.5k–362k. The blob's time extent is T_univ = π s̃0 N41^{1/4}. Curves collapse when N3 is scaled by N4^{3/4} and time by N4^{1/4}.

targets.title: Hausdorff dimension from the volume–volume correlator

items.label: Definition
items.text: C(δ) = Σ_τ 4⟨(N3(τ)−s/2)(N3(τ+δ)−s/2)⟩/(Ñ4 − t·s)², with s ≈ 25.5. It is normalised so that Σ_δ C(δ) = 1.

items.label: Scaling form
items.text: c(x) = (Ñ4^eff)^{1/D_H} C((Ñ4^eff)^{1/D_H} x), with Ñ4^eff = Ñ4 − t·s.

items.label: Result
items.text: best overlap gives D_H ≈ 3.8 ± 0.25 for Ñ4 = 10k–160k, using T=80.

items.label: Diffusion rule
items.text: K(j; σ+1) = (1/5) Σ_{k→j} K(k; σ) over the 5 neighbours on the dual graph of pentachora (no laziness). It starts from a single (4,1)-simplex adjacent to the slice of maximal N3.

items.label: Spectral dimension
items.text: P(σ) = K(i0, i0; σ) and D_S = −2 d log P/d log σ. Only σ ≥ 40 is used, because the odd and even values of σ differ for σ ≲ 20–30.

items.label: Result
items.text: at N4 = 181k (Ñ4 = 80k), T=80, averaged over 400 diffusion processes, D_S(σ) = 4.02 − 119/(54+σ) on σ ∈ [40, 400]. So D_S(∞) = 4.02 ± 0.1 and D_S(0) = 1.80 ± 0.25.

items.label: Finite size
items.text: for Ñ4 = 20k and 40k, D_S(σ) peaks and then falls at large σ ([R] Fig. 9). The curves envelop the infinite-volume curve from below.

items.label: Covariance and propagator
items.text: C(i,j) is the covariance of the centred profiles. It has a zero mode because ΣN3 is fixed. P̂ is the inverse of C on the space orthogonal to the zero mode.

items.label: Fit
items.text: P̂ ≈ P̂_kin + P̂_pot, with P̂_kin = Σ_i p_i X^(i) (nearest-neighbour Laplacian-like) and P̂_pot a projected diagonal matrix. This is a least-χ² fit of tr(P̂ − P̂_kin − P̂_pot)².

items.label: Result
items.text: k1 = 0.038, independent of N41 over 20k–160k at (2.2, 0.6). The potential term is noisy and contaminated by the stalk.
